title: No fixed compatible $H^1$-system on a proper curve
statement:
Let $C_0/\mathbf F_Q$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected
curve, put $C=C_0\times_{\mathbf F_Q}\overline{\mathbf F}_Q$, and put
$A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, where $\ell$ is a prime and $\ell\nmid Q$. Then

$$
\left(\varprojlim_nH^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,A_n)\right)^{\Phi_Q=1}=0,
\tag{4.4}
$$

The inverse limit is the ordinary inverse limit for the coefficient reduction maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Write $\sigma_Q:z\mapsto z^Q$ and $\gamma_Q=\sigma_Q^{-1}$. Here $\Phi_Q$ acts at each finite level by pullback along the geometric Galois Frobenius $g_C=\operatorname{id}_{C_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma_Q)$ of [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], using the canonical identification of the pullback of the constant sheaf $A_n$ with $A_n$. The finite-level cohomology is that of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text:
Put $H=\varprojlim_nH^1(C,A_n)$. Choose the geometric Jacobian $J$ with the canonical Galois action supplied by [lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action], and put $T=T_\ell J$. Apply [lem-wf-curve-h1-dual-tate-module] over $k_0=\mathbf F_Q$: the curve is smooth projective geometrically connected and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, so its natural Galois-equivariant isomorphism identifies $H$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(T,\mathbf Z_\ell)$. The action on this dual is $(\tau f)(t)=f(\tau^{-1}t)$, since evaluation into the trivial Galois module $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is equivariant. By [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], the geometric operator in the statement is the action of $\gamma_Q=\sigma_Q^{-1}$. Thus if $x\in H$ is fixed by $\Phi_Q$, its image $f$ satisfies
$$f(\sigma_Qt)=f(t),\qquad f((\sigma_Q-1)t)=0\quad(t\in T).$$
This uses the twisted pairing only through the cited integral Galois-equivariant comparison; there is no identification of twisted and untwisted cohomology.

source.place: First paragraph: geometric Frobenius and the Galois-equivariant dual-Tate identification

proof.text:
By [lem-wf-finite-field-tate-no-fixed], $\sigma_Q-1$ is an automorphism of $V_\ell J$. Its curve and prime hypotheses are exactly those already in force. The definitions [def-wf-abelian-tate-module] and [def-tate-module-abelian-group] identify this space with $T[1/\ell]$, with the componentwise action extended to fractions. For any $t\in T$, surjectivity gives $v=\ell^{-b}u$ with $(\sigma_Q-1)v=t/1$, for some $b\ge0$ and $u\in T$. The stated equality criterion for fractions gives $d\ge0$ such that
$$\ell^d((\sigma_Q-1)u-\ell^bt)=0\quad\text{in }T.$$
Applying the linear functional $f$ and the equality from Step 1 yields $\ell^{b+d}f(t)=0$. This argument requires neither a basis of $T$ nor an injectivity assertion for its map to the localization.

source.place: Second paragraph: rational invertibility of arithmetic Frobenius minus one; denominators cleared explicitly using the existing rational clause

proof.text: The ring of compatible residues $\mathbf Z_\ell$ in [def-tate-module-abelian-group] has no $\ell$-power torsion: if $\ell^ac=0$, its residue at level $n+a$ is killed by $\ell^a$, hence is divisible by $\ell^n$ in $\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+a}\mathbf Z$. Reduction to level $n$ gives $c_n=0$ for every $n\ge1$, so $c=0$. Apply this to $c=f(t)$ and $a=b+d$ from Step 2. Thus $f(t)=0$ for all $t\in T$, whence $f=0$. The isomorphism of Step 1 is injective, so $x=0$. Every fixed compatible system is therefore zero, as asserted.
